text.p: Italian debt futures charged to fresh record highs in late European trading on Friday, while the lira, finishing its first week back in the ERM, was up in territory not seen for more than two years.

The December BTP futures contract on LIFFE, which expires next Wednesday, tore to a peak of 128.91, outstripping the 128.70 high set on November 25. By 1620 GMT it was trading 108 basis points higher on the day at 128.85.
The lira, which rejoined Europe's exchange mechanism last weekend, finished the week with a flourish as it strengthend to 984.10 per mark, an area not seen since early July 1994.
The July 2006 Btp ended 95 basis points up at 109.28, with the yield at 7.51 percent and the spread over 10-year Bunds out at 188 basis points from the 171 area seen earlier in the week.
Brokers said however much volume on the futures was rollover operations from the December to the March contracts. The March contract was 108 basis points higher at 127.92.
Brokers said the charge higher was a Europe-wide move rather than being specific to Btps but given this latest blast, some saw scope for Btp futures to move up to 130 and beyond.
"There are just no sellers out there. People have got sucked into positions they don't want to hold," one broker said.

Traders said the surge had been fuelled by talk -- which they were highly sceptical about -- of a coordinated rate cut by Germany and France. While they were highly wary of the motive behind the rallies, they pointed out players could not afford to ignore the gains.

At home earlier, the Treasury auctioned 2.0 trillion lire of three-year Btps and 2.0 trillion lire of five-year Btps, with gross yields rising to 6.34 and 6.73 percent from 6.13 and 6.5 percent respectively and both meeting reasonable demand.
